storyTitle: Islington councillors demand consistent cyclist safety measures during roadworks
headline: Islington demands safer cycle lanes during roadworks
committee: Environment, Climate and Transport Scrutiny Committee Islington, 20 October 2026
keyPointsHeading: Why do cycle safety rules vary?

watchability.hook: Islington demands safer cycle lanes during roadworks
watchability.hookStyle: Immediate factual council decision and resident impact
watchability.localRelevance: Directly affects Islington residents and council services

claims.statement: Councillors highlighted inconsistent safety measures for cyclists across different roadwork sites in Islington.
claims.sourceQuote: Councillor Sophia Brown highlighted inconsistencies, pointing to differing approaches at Middleton Square and Highbury Grove.
claims.sourceDocument: Environment, Climate and Transport Scrutiny Committee Islington, 20 October 2026

claims.statement: Two-way cycling on Highbury Grove could not be maintained due to road width constraints.
claims.sourceQuote: For Highbury Grove, the council determined that maintaining two-way cycling would require a 3-meter space, which, with a half-meter safety zone and accounting for general traffic lane reduction, would create a 3-meter space. This was deemed insufficient, as the council's guidance suggests a minimum of 3.5 meters for buses and 2.75 meters for general traffic.
claims.sourceDocument: Environment, Climate and Transport Scrutiny Committee Islington, 20 October 2026

claims.statement: The council conceded that dismount signs fail to support cyclists using bikes as mobility aids.
claims.sourceQuote: The council acknowledged the challenge for these cyclists, stating that 'cyclist dismount' signs are not an acceptable solution and that longer detours are being forced upon people with accessibility needs.
claims.sourceDocument: Environment, Climate and Transport Scrutiny Committee Islington, 20 October 2026

takeawayCard.title: Dismount signs face council review
takeawayCard.subtitle: Officers will review rules for mobility aid users.

keyPoints: Maintaining two-way cycling at Highbury Grove required 3.0 metres of unavailable space.
Council guidance mandates a minimum width of 3.5 metres for bus traffic.
Contractors must preserve 2.75 metres for general traffic alongside work safety zones.

timeline.voiceoverText: Tight road layouts require 3.5 metres for buses and 2.75 metres for cars, restricting safe cycle lanes.
With minimum widths squeezing out cyclists, the council has committed to reviewing detours for mobility aid users.
